notable_features.text: Mandarin is a tonal language in which pitch contour distinguishes word meaning, and it follows a basic subject-verb-object word order. It encodes a notably rich set of tense/aspect distinctions (7 WALS categories) despite lacking inflectional morphology, relying instead on particles and word order. As a pluricentric language, it has standardized but accentually and lexically distinct varieties used officially across Mainland China, Taiwan, and Singapore.
